first.rationale: I currently intend to test onboarding simplification because completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence suggests reducing friction improves time-to-value and SMB activation. I would verify the onboarding result and the competing promotional-pricing result because both are consequential to this week's choice, while their durability and contribution to sustainable qualified revenue are not fully established. The test should be guarded and judged on qualified activation and downstream revenue, not completion alone, since simpler onboarding could increase low-intent signups without improving valuable accounts.

final.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding-simplification experiment this week. The verified result shows materially higher completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Measure qualified activation, time-to-value, retention, and qualified revenue—not completion alone. Do not select promotional pricing: although it lifted qualified revenue 18% initially, 30-day retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle.
